scope: A convenience panel of four contemporary Russian prose authors, writing dates 1890–1904, explicit digital witnesses. It is not a representative sample of Russian literature.

selection.genre: Russian narrative fiction: stories and short novellas; no plays, verse, essays, composite collections or the Chekhov little trilogy
selection.selection_basis: Public source/date availability and length before any model fit. Quotas reflect available contemporary works; no selection by recognition results.
selection.locked_test_rule: All locked-test title identities are absent from the historical 252-work corrected panel. Roles are fixed before new development or locked-test fits.

source_limitations: Print edition labels and writing dates are declarations of the public digital provider. No scan collation or archival authentication was performed.
HTML and extracted UTF-8 hashes attest the freshly acquired digital witnesses only. They do not authenticate the historical corpus bytes or establish disputed literary authorship.
All witnesses come from one digital provider. Print source editions are substantially associated with author; this panel cannot isolate author style from edition/source effects.
New held-out works provide independent work-level evaluation in this declared panel, not transfer across providers, new periods, genres, or absent authors.
One provider is not a license to redistribute text. Only bibliography, acquisition recipes, hashes and aggregates are committed; raw HTML and extracted texts remain ignored local inputs.

Historical content comparisons reuse retained local inputs, not independently sourced historical editions. One historical input is below the 20-shingle minimum and is explicitly excluded from ordinary near-copy assurance.

extraction.paragraph_rule: Direct-child <z> paragraphs of div#text, preserving inline prose; separate headers, author/title labels, chapter headings, navigation, dates and notes omitted; superscript note markers omitted.
extraction.whitespace_rule: Collapse whitespace within each paragraph, join nonempty paragraphs and chapters with two LF, append one final LF.
extraction.additional_normalization: None. Model-side normalisation is applied subsequently by the comparison runner.
extraction.word_count_method: Unicode letter runs, optionally joined by internal -, ’, or ' (Python regex [^\W\d_]+(?:[-’'][^\W\d_]+)*). This is not a spaCy token count.
extraction.html_sha256_semantics: Hashes record acquired HTML renderings. The provider changes service markup on refetch; reconstruction verifies the exact processed body hash, exact declared edition/date labels and complete chapter URL inventory. Actual rendering hashes and drift are recorded separately.

historical_exposure_check.review_policy: Full author-level historical work-ID lists were inspected. Cyrillic/transliterated title aliases were matched manually; differing spelling, punctuation, and ё/е are not evidence of a new work. No new edition of a known title is counted as novel.

content_overlap_audit.method: stylo.domain.corpus_identity._word_shingles; exact word-5 set intersection / smaller set
content_overlap_audit.interpretation: No >=0.90 containment means no near-copy found by this lexical check; it does not prove thematic, stylistic, editorial or archival independence.

locked_vs_historical.below_minimum_interpretation: Exact intersections are computed, but inputs below 20 unique shingles cannot support the ordinary near-copy absence claim for a literary work.

fresh_network_reconstruction.bibliographic_labels_and_complete_chapte: All 33 match acquired declarations and chapter URL lists.
fresh_network_reconstruction.identity_binding: Fresh receipt IDs and processed hashes are identical to this manifest; receipt precedes the addition of audit summaries and explicit edition-year fields.
fresh_network_reconstruction.network_warnings: An initial attempt timed out; complete fresh retry passed. Provider rendering HTML changed on all pages while bibliographic labels and processed bodies remained stable.
